title: THE SAME PATTERN, A SMALLER GIFT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If the offering is a burnt offering from the flock, from either the sheep or the goats, you are to offer a male without defect. You are to slaughter it at the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall splash its blood against the sides of the altar.'" - Lev 1:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter moves from bulls to sheep and goats — from the offering of a wealthy man to something a family of modest means could manage. Notice what changes and what does not.

What changes: the size of the animal. What stays the same: without defect, slaughtered before the LORD, blood splashed on the altar, accepted as atonement.

God scaled the cost to the worshipper's ability without scaling down the standard of holiness. The poorer Israelite was not given a second-class relationship with God. His lamb was received with exactly the same seriousness as his neighbour's bull.

This should quietly demolish a lie that many believers carry — that God values the people who can give more, do more, serve more. He does not. Jesus watched a widow drop in two small coins and said she had given more than all the rest (Mk 12:43-44). The measure is not the amount; it is the heart behind it.

So do not compare your offering to anyone else's. Do not think your smaller life, smaller income, smaller platform makes you less welcome at the altar. God has never operated on that basis.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I secretly measure my worth to God by what I am able to give Him?
2. Whose offering am I comparing mine to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, free me from measuring myself against others in my walk with You. Receive what I have, small as it may be, and let it be truly Yours. Amen.
